messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High p95/p99 latency on /v1/generate (hosted) · triggered by autoscaler in rg-prod-us-west. Error rate up ~1.8% → 3.6% over 5m. Pager sent to #eng-oncall.
aran (oncall): seeing it, jumping in. confirming p95 ~1200ms, p99 ~3100ms on text-gen; baseline is p95 220ms.
kim (sre): adding the top-line metrics: CPU on gs-rt-4 spike to 95%, GPU utilization 98% on pool-a. Continuous batching queue depth increased.
lucy (eng-ml): timeline: we pushed a new batching tuning change in canary ~2h ago that increased batch_{max_latency_ms} from 8 -> 20 to improve throughput. Canary looked fine but maybe under different traffic shape.
aran (oncall): ok possible root cause: continuous batching waiting longer to fill batches -> larger batch sizes -> longer token latency for tail requests. Need live mitigation.
kevin (night-oncall): what's customer impact? any SEV1s or big customers complaining?
mia (support): several customers reported timeouts in the last 10m; one enterprise dashboarding client got ~10k 504s in 12m and filed a ticket. I'll mark high and attach logs.
lucy (eng-ml): quick assessment: tradeoff options: revert batching param to previous (max_latency_ms=8), reduce batch_max_size, or route traffic to dedicated quantized variant (v2-q8) which queues better. Also can temporarily disable streaming which reduces per-request overhead.
kim (sre): we should prefer param change over deploy rollback. It's faster and less risky. Also consider global rate limit on non-enterprise orgs to reduce load.
aran (oncall): proposed immediate mitigations (live): 1) increase batching max latency back to 8ms (i.e., revert recent change) 2) apply per-org rate limit to free tier to 1r/s 3) enable `prefer_small_batches` flag on pool-a 4) temporarily disable streaming chunked responses for text-gen routes while further testing occurs. Which one should we do first?
lucy (eng-ml): do param revert first — low-risk, instant. I can push a config override. I'll also queue the quantized model fallback if revert doesn't help.
kim (sre): I'll open a traffic-shaper ticket and prepare an iptable-like shaper to cap inbound QPS from noisy sources.
aran (oncall): mia please draft a customer-facing note: "We're investigating increased latency on text generation endpoints; mitigations in progress."
mia (support): on it, posting now to affected customers and the status page.
lucy (eng-ml): config change command (internal):
```bash
# set continuous batching max_latency back to 8ms on pool-a
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/pools/pool-a/config \
  -d '{"continuous_batching":{"max_latency_ms":8}}'
```
I will run this.
deploy-bot: deploy job 48219 queued by lucy — config patch -> pool-a (canary)
lucy (eng-ml): applied override to pool-a canary, rolling to pool-a-1..4 sequentially.
aran (oncall): rolling to whole pool? careful, do steady step. start canary then wait 60s and watch p95.
kim (sre): watching metrics: 30s after canary -> p95 dropped 220ms? pulling dashboards... yes p95 down to 260ms on canary nodes, p99 still ~700ms.
aran (oncall): good sign. continue roll.
lucy (eng-ml): rolling rest of pool now.
kim (sre): p95 global trending down. error rate also dropping from 3.6% -> 1.2%.
aran (oncall): still see a small group of high-QPS orgs spiking. let's enable per-org soft-limits for non-enterprise.
kim (sre): applying per-org rate-limiter via gateway rule:
```json
{"match":{"org_id":"*","tier":"free"},"limit":{"qps":1}}
```
applied to edge-gw-2.
deploy-bot: policy applied on edge-gw-2 by kim.
mia (support): affected customers list updated. free-tier customers will see degraded throughput; enterprise customers not affected. Posting to status page: "Rate limits applied to free-tier to protect platform".
kevin (night-oncall): are we disabling streaming yet? that's more intrusive but might reduce load by ~8-12% CPU.
lucy (eng-ml): I recommend keeping streaming on for enterprise; disable for free-tier only. How to do that quickly: config toggle at route level.
lucy (eng-ml): command to flip streaming off for free tier:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routes/text-gen/config \
  -d '{"streaming":{"enabled":false,"selector":"tier==\"free\""}}'
```
kim (sre): I've staged the toggle in canary, no regressions. If safe, flip globally for free tier.
aran (oncall): go ahead. lucy/k im coordinate.
lucy (eng-ml): toggled streaming off for free-tier across region us-west.
kim (sre): immediate effect: request CPU down ~6%, p95 improved further to 210ms, p99 ~360ms. Error rate down to 0.6%.
aran (oncall): great. next mitigation: prepare fallback routing to quantized v2-q8 for non-enterprise and burst traffic. lucy can you prepare route?
lucy (eng-ml): creating fallback route: prefer v2-q8 when queue_depth > 1000 or pool util > 92%. Will push rule now.
lucy (eng-ml): rule pushed.
deploy-bot: fallback routing rule 77422 active on rg-prod-us-west.
kim (sre): monitoring: pool utilization now leveling ~82%, overall throughput stable. Mythic dashboards show decrease in tail latency.
aran (oncall): customer impact summary for postmortem: - Duration: ~30m of elevated latency, peak p95 1.2s, p99 3.1s - Affected: primarily free-tier and a small set of mid-tier bursty customers - Root cause: tuning change to continuous_batching.max_latency_ms increased batching waiting time which under a bursty, burst+spike traffic shape created very large batches and resource saturation - Mitigations: reverted config, applied per-org rate limits for free-tier, disabled streaming for free-tier, enabled fallback to quantized variant - Current status: mitigated, metrics stabilized.
mia (support): I've emailed the enterprise customer that reported 504s with explanation and next steps. They accept temporary impact and asked for postmortem.
kevin (night-oncall): handoff: I'm taking night shift starting 2145007000 — will monitor. Aran, any known follow-ups?
\aran (oncall): I'll remain available until 2145007050 for questions. Follow-ups: schedule a rollback of the canary change in the repo, add a test to our canary traffic harness that simulates bursty short requests, and tune the continuous batching controller to cap max_batch_size based on observed tail latency.
lucy (eng-ml): I'll open a PR to add adaptive_max_batch_size logic (limit by recent tail latency) and revert the last canary change.
kim (sre): create a runbook note: when p99>1000ms, revert continuous_batching.max_latency_ms -> 8ms and consider disabling streaming for free-tier.
aran (oncall): closing the pager as mitigated. Leaving an incident summary in incidents channel and opening a postmortem ticket.
incident-bot: Pager closed by aran — incident status: mitigated — severity: Sev2 — incident_id: INC-2026-2145
mi a (support): typo? (bot)
kevin (night-oncall): lol, all good. I'll keep an eye on the quantized fallback latencies overnight. If it behaves poorly we can revert fallback route.
lucy (eng-ml): noted; I'll run an overnight perf job to gather batch shape distributions.
aran (oncall): thanks team. If anything flares, @kevin escalate to eng-sre. Good job.
